clue.text: Change the country, switching between this and that?

parts.note: to change something is to alter it
a country is a nation

explanation.surface: Someone urges reform of their homeland, wondering whether to keep flipping between two options.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like the definition, but it is ALTER, and the definition is the question at the end; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Going back and forth between two options is alternation, a regular swap from one to the other.

clue.text: Melissa sadly lacking purpose

indicators.note: sadly suggests the letters of the name are in a sorry, disordered state

explanation.surface: A woman called Melissa is unfortunately drifting through life without goals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges MELISSA into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done without aim or goal is directionless, the exact sense of lacking purpose.

clue.text: Supernatural creature? He is missing from the list

indicators.note: says the word He is taken out of the phrase that follows it

parts.note: taken as written
a roll is a list of names, as in a register

explanation.surface: Someone checks a register and finds a man's name absent, then wonders about a magical being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is missing from' removes HE from THE ROLL, leaving T + ROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scandinavian folklore a troll is an ugly giant or dwarf, a creature of myth.

clue.text: Following all others, I have to be uneasy

indicators.note: says the piece for I have comes after the piece for all others

parts.note: the rest means all the others
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone who comes last behind everyone feels restless about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' places the contraction of 'I have' after the word for all others; 'to be' is a link, so the definition is just 'uneasy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Restive describes someone fidgety and unable to settle, a synonym of uneasy.

clue.text: The country's new regalia

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of regalia are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A nation unveils fresh crown jewels and royal insignia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges REGALIA; the 's after 'The country' stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is a North African state, an example of a nation.

clue.text: Home team has man suffering on account of a type of crime

parts.note: being home is being in
a team is a side
Job is the Biblical man who suffered great afflictions

explanation.surface: A home football side has a player in pain, and that somehow becomes a criminal matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home team' reads as one sports idea but splits in two; Job is the long-suffering man of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A theft carried out by someone working at the victim's premises is called an inside job, a category of criminal act.

clue.text: William's men giving standard answer

parts.note: a norm is a standard

explanation.surface: A man named William gets a conventional reply from his followers.
explanation.walkthrough: William is William the Conqueror, whose followers invaded England in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: The Normans were the forces of William the Conqueror at the Battle of Hastings.

clue.text: College food for a government house

definitions.meaning: shared rations provided in a university college
the lower chamber of the UK Parliament

explanation.surface: Student dining is set beside a chamber of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: At some British universities the shared meals provided by a college are called commons; the lower house of the UK Parliament is the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: College meals eaten in common hall carry this name, and so does the elected lower chamber at Westminster.

clue.text: Like fortification bill set up with girl and boy

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the piece for bill is turned to read upwards

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
Stella is a girl's name
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A castle-like structure is somehow invoiced together with a young couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns the bill upwards, as suits a down clue; the girl and boy are just common first names.
explanation.definitionFit: A castellated building has battlements and turrets as a castle does, so it resembles defensive works.

clue.text: Little Mary's empty talk, deceitful device mostly

parts.note: gas is idle, empty chatter

indicators.note: mostly means the word is used without its final letter

parts.note: a trick is a deceitful device

explanation.surface: A girl called Mary chatters idly and plays a sneaky prank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Mary' is old British slang for the stomach; 'mostly' trims TRICK to TRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastric means relating to the stomach, which old slang called little Mary.

clue.text: Sudden disaster can be sorted out by Prescott? Aha!

indicators.note: sorted out suggests the letters of the two words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A politician named Prescott solves a calamity and exclaims in triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted out' rearranges PRESCOTT and AHA together; John Prescott was a British deputy prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe is a calamity, an abrupt and terrible event.

clue.text: To be a thief needs extreme hardness, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: steel is a byword for great hardness

explanation.surface: Becoming a burglar requires being tough as nails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' turns STEEL, the metal standing for hardness, into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is taking property unlawfully, the very act of a thief.

clue.text: Bright characters perversely participating in train raid

indicators.note: perversely means the letters are arranged in a contrary, wayward order

explanation.surface: Clever people take part in a railway robbery, wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perversely' rearranges the letters of TRAIN RAID; 'characters' and 'participating in' are links pointing to those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Irradiant means shining or emitting light, a synonym of bright.

clue.text: I use net possibly for the bathroom

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a mesh might be handy in the washroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges I USE NET; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An en suite is a bathroom attached to a bedroom, from the French for 'in sequence'.

clue.text: Reviled in audible attack

indicators.note: audible shows the word for attack is to be heard, giving a different spelling

parts.note: to invade is to attack a territory

explanation.surface: Someone was abused in a noisy assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audible' makes INVADE sound like the answer; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To inveigh is to rail or speak bitterly against, so the past tense means denounced.

clue.text: Modifies commercials — contents must be fair

indicators.note: contents says one piece is held inside the other, as what a container holds

parts.note: ads are commercials
just means fair

explanation.surface: An advertising watchdog insists every advert inside must be honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents' says the fair word goes inside the commercials; 'must be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust something is to alter it slightly, a synonym of modifies.

clue.text: Having had interruptions from Henry and Rex, leave port

indicators.note: says the word leave is broken into at more than one point by the letters that follow
from marks where the second interrupting letter comes from, each letter entering leave separately

parts.note: taken as written
H is the symbol for henry, the unit of inductance
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone, having been interrupted by two men, departs from a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having had interruptions' and 'from' put H and R into LEAVE at two separate places, LE-H-AV-R-E; 'and' is a link. The surface makes 'leave' a verb, but it is the word to be broken into.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Havre is a major seaport in Normandy, northern France.

clue.text: Thrifty manager in hard American group

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
US means American
a band is a group

explanation.surface: A careful steward works within a tough US pop group.
explanation.walkthrough: The old sense of the word is a careful manager of resources, as in husbanding supplies; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In its older sense the word means someone who manages a household or resources economically.

clue.text: Leave the country — but no good being in an Arab state

indicators.note: no says the letter for good is to be absent

parts.note: to emigrate is to leave one's country to live abroad

explanation.surface: Someone thinks of moving abroad, but warns it is useless living in a Gulf kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes G from EMIGRATE; 'but' and 'being in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An emirate is a state ruled by an emir, such as those in the UAE.

clue.text: Seafood? Throw back all but the last bit

parts.note: to lob is to throw

indicators.note: all but the last bit means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone tosses food back into the sea, keeping only the tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like part of 'Throw back' but gives STERN, trimmed by 'all but the last bit' to STER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobster is a shellfish eaten as a delicacy, an example of food from the ocean.

clue.text: Strong desire — odd going on for five years!

parts.note: lust is strong desire
rum means odd in British slang

explanation.surface: A peculiar passion has lasted half a decade.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM is British informal for strange; 'going on for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lustrum is a span of five years, originally the Roman census period.

clue.text: Artist favoured getting external support for apprentice

indicators.note: getting external says the support piece goes around the outside of the others

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
in means favoured or fashionable

explanation.surface: A popular painter backs a young learner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting external' wraps the golfer's support around the artist and favoured pieces; a Royal Academician is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is someone learning a trade, a synonym of apprentice.

clue.text: Is a witness to condition that is part of the international sports match

indicators.note: part of says the condition and that is pieces are placed within the match word

parts.note: Tests are international cricket or rugby matches, here taken in the plural as a series
if introduces a condition
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone gives evidence about a rule in a cricket Test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' places the condition and 'that is' pieces inside Tests, international cricket or rugby matches; the setter needs the plural; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify is to give evidence, so the verb means acts as a witness.

clue.text: Pile of potatoes left in military station

indicators.note: in says the letter for left sits inside the station

parts.note: a camp is a military station

explanation.surface: Soldiers store a heap of spuds at their base.
explanation.walkthrough: A clamp is a mound of root vegetables stored under earth and straw, a farming term.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamp is a stack of potatoes or other root crops covered for storage.

clue.text: Small part arrived with ring attached

parts.note: came means arrived
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone turned up wearing a ring for a minor role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'attached' are links joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a brief appearance by a well-known actor, a minor role.

clue.text: Church in tense situation — not much money

indicators.note: in says the letters for church sit inside the other word

parts.note: a drama is an exciting, tense situation

explanation.surface: A tense crisis in a church over a tiny sum.
explanation.walkthrough: The drachma was the Greek currency before the euro, and in ancient Greece a small coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A drachma was a coin of modest value, so it stands for a small amount of cash.

clue.text: Some hero, man celebrated in fictional tale

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hero gets feted in a storybook.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'in', which is a link: 'in fictional tale' cannot stand for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a story of adventure or love, an imaginative narrative.

clue.text: Former comedian from Midlands town, terrible Romeo

parts.note: Dudley is a town in the English West Midlands

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters of Romeo are badly mangled

explanation.surface: An ex-comic from the Midlands gives an awful performance as Shakespeare's lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges ROMEO; Dudley Moore was an English comedian and actor; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudley Moore, who died in 2002, was a famous comic performer.
